balance.argument_a: Ring Alpha's dense adjacency-matrix block (24 of 45 possible connections in the illustrative sample, 53.3% density) is a real, published bot-ring signature, and connectivity signal is comparatively insensitive to a one-time traffic surge -- unlike a volume threshold, a bot ring's mutual-follow pattern does not suddenly look different because real users are also posting more this weekend. Modeled at Appendix E's rates, suspending Ring Alpha removes 4.00 confirmed bots for every real account wrongly caught.
balance.argument_b: Wave Nine's posting-volume signal is, in ordinary conditions, the real stronger individual predictor -- content/volume features alone reach a real published AUC above 0.90 (S1), better than connectivity features alone (AUC above 0.80, S1) -- and Wave Nine's own accounts mostly target real users rather than each other, meaning Ring Alpha's dense block, however textbook it looks, is also textbook-consistent with a real tight-knit creator collab group (S3's real 60.55% local clustering coefficient shows ordinary real friend circles cluster nearly this densely too). Modeled at Appendix E's surge-adjusted rates, suspending Wave Nine still removes 3.44 confirmed bots per real account wrongly caught -- a real, sourced, working alternative, not a clearly inferior one.
balance.margin_basis: Primary metric = confirmed-bot accounts removed / real accounts wrongly suspended, for each cluster, using Appendix E's modeled false-positive rates (MA6, MA7 -- both derived from Appendix D's real published combined-system false-positive rate, S1). Algebraically, this ratio equals (1 - p)/p, where p is the cluster's modeled false-positive rate -- it does NOT depend on cluster size (MA4/MA5 cancel out completely). Ring Alpha: (1-0.20)/0.20 = 4.00. Wave Nine: (1-0.225)/0.225 = 3.44 (repeating). margin_pct = (4.00 - 3.44)/4.00 x 100 = 13.9%.
balance.margin_pct_note: COMPUTED 2026-09-01 (case-research), well under SPEC Section 2's ~20% cap on the first construction -- no retune pass was needed. Counterfactual check (does the surge-premium modeling choice, MA7, actually drive the result?): if Wave Nine's false-positive rate were left at Appendix D's real, UNSCALED baseline (15%, i.e. no surge premium at all), its ratio would be (1-0.15)/0.15 = 5.67 -- beating Ring Alpha's 4.00 by a real margin of (5.67-4.00)/5.67 x 100 = 29.4%, flipping the recommendation to Option B. So this case's real fulcrum is MA7 (whether volume-based detection's real-world false-positive rate is elevated by the surge), not cluster size, not Ring Alpha's own rate in isolation, and not which cluster is bigger. This is disclosed explicitly in FACILITATOR.md's Twist material.

Maximum clusters safely suspendable per incident
modeling_assumptions.basis: Scenario constraint that forces the binary choice.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Structural -- without it there is no dilemma.

modeling_assumptions.claim: Ring Alpha accounts flagged this incident
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: NONE on margin_pct -- the primary-metric ratio (1-p)/p is independent of cluster size; proven algebraically in balance.margin_basis.

modeling_assumptions.claim: Wave Nine accounts flagged this incident
modeling_assumptions.basis: Illustrative in-scenario cluster size, independently sized from Ring Alpha's.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: NONE on margin_pct -- same reasoning as MA4.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Derived from Appendix D's real published combined-system false-positive rate (0.15, S1), scaled up ~30% and rounded, reflecting connectivity-only detection's real, published lower standalone AUC (>0.80, S1) vs. the full system (0.95 AUC, S1).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: MODERATE-HIGH. At the real unscaled baseline (15%), Ring Alpha's ratio would tie Wave Nine's ordinary-conditions ratio at 5.67.

modeling_assumptions.claim: Wave Nine's modeled false-positive rate, surge conditions
modeling_assumptions.basis: Derived from the same real 0.15 baseline (S1), scaled up 50%. Volume/content detection alone reaches a real higher standalone AUC (>0.90, S1) than connectivity alone in ordinary conditions -- but a real traffic surge raises real users' own posting volume too, a general, industry-documented limitation of volume-based anomaly rules during high-traffic windows.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: HIGH -- the single most dilemma-relevant modeling choice. Removing the surge premium (back to 15%) flips the winner to Wave Nine by a real 29.4% margin.

modeling_assumptions.claim: Wave Nine's average sustained posting rate, this incident
modeling_assumptions.basis: Chosen to sit close to (but under) Appendix F's real published ~400 posts/hour technical ceiling (S2).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: LOW -- flavor/context only; does not enter the primary-metric computation.

sensitivity_note: margin_pct (13.9%) is comfortably under SPEC Section 2's ~20% cap, computed from a genuinely clean structural fact: the primary metric's ratio, confirmed-bots/false-positives = (1-p)/p, is provably independent of the two clusters' flagged-account counts (MA4, MA5) -- only the two modeled false-positive rates (MA6, MA7) matter. Of those two, MA7 (Wave Nine's surge-elevated rate) is the real fulcrum: reverting it to the real, unscaled academic baseline (15%, no surge premium) flips the recommendation to Option B by a real 29.4% margin. This is the case's actual twist material -- see FACILITATOR.md and sensitivity_model.py.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA6 (Ring Alpha's false-positive rate, 20%) is derived by scaling S1's real published combined-system baseline (15%) up ~30%; case.md's own table computes the counterfactual at the real unscaled 15% baseline explicitly (ratio 0.85/0.15=5.67) and states this would tie Wave Nine's ordinary-conditions ratio -- a disclosed, not hidden, calibration choice.

MA7 (Wave Nine's false-positive rate, 22.5% surge-scaled) is flagged 'the single most dilemma-relevant modeling choice in the case' in case.md, which explicitly states that at the real unscaled baseline (15%, no surge premium) the recommendation flips to Option B by ~29% -- this exact flip is documented and is the case's own designed Twist mechanism, not an undisclosed instability.
